requirement: SAP IDs run from 0 to 15, so at most 16 clients can use the SIS of one node.
notes: Same in Ed4 S.1.2.

requirement: Clients may reach the SIS through the Annex S access protocol, directly, or by another protocol.
notes: Annex S itself makes its mechanism mandatory for servers (Ed4 S.1.2, p.S-2); we offer Annex S.

requirement: Clients, not the SIS, split large messages into U_PDUs.
notes: The SIS never segments client data.

requirement: The SIS treats every client the same way whatever its application.
Two session types exist: a Soft Link Data Exchange Session, which needs a point-to-point physical link, and a Broadcast Data Exchange Session, which gives unreliable transfer with no physical link.
notes: Text cross references to "A.1.1.x" elsewhere in Annex A are stale; the numbers are A.1.3 to A.1.5.

requirement: Clients may interleave requests needing different session types.
Local management may restrict a node to a single session type, for example broadcast only.
reason: optional; we offer no broadcast-only or single-session-type configuration (general-purpose node)

requirement: The SIS that holds queued ARQ U_PDUs initiates a soft link session unilaterally.
Soft links may also be started for non-ARQ traffic over ALE links when the CAS asks for one.
reason: ALE not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: The SIS initiates soft link sessions as needed using the procedure of A.3.2.1.
When all data for a soft-linked node has been sent, the SIS terminates the session after a configurable, implementation-dependent timeout, per A.3.2.1.3.
Soft link termination follows the procedure of A.3.2.1.3.
The idle timeout before termination may be zero.
notes: The timeout lets newly arriving U_PDUs use the existing link.

requirement: For balanced service, a soft link session is not kept beyond a specified maximum time while U_PDUs of suitable priority are queued for other nodes.
notes: Under MSPA several soft links may be open at once; the limit still applies where the CAS or DTS cannot serve the other node in parallel.

requirement: The maximum soft link session time is a configurable parameter.
During a Broadcast Data Exchange Session the subnetwork serves only clients needing non-ARQ U_PDUs.
reason: we never enter an exclusive Broadcast Data Exchange Session; under MSPA non-ARQ is sent without a soft link alongside ARQ traffic (A.3.2.1.1)

requirement: Clients needing non-ARQ U_PDUs may also be served during other session types, according to that session's service characteristics.
A management process (local or network administrator client) may start and end a Broadcast Data Exchange Session.
reason: no exclusive broadcast session offered (general-purpose node)

requirement: Procedures that start and end broadcast sessions are those of Annex C.
notes: See C matrix for non-ARQ procedures.

requirement: A broadcast-only node uses a permanent Broadcast Data Exchange Session.
reason: our node is general-purpose, not broadcast-only

requirement: During that permanent broadcast session the SIS serves no ARQ U_PDUs.
reason: our node is general-purpose, not broadcast-only

requirement: The SIS may instead start and end broadcast sessions on its own initiative.
notes: In practice: the SIS sends non-ARQ U_PDUs whenever it chooses.

requirement: The core broadcast service delivers only error-free data.
Delivery of data that may contain errors is the optional NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS profile option.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Where Table A-1 and the detailed primitive sections differ, the detailed sections govern.

Table A-1 core primitives: client to SIS S_BIND_REQUEST, S_UNBIND_REQUEST, S_UNIDATA_REQUEST; SIS to client S_BIND_ACCEPTED, S_BIND_REJECTED, S_UNBIND_INDICATION, S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM, S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED, S_UNIDATA_INDICATION.
notes: Encodings in Ed4 S.5.

requirement: Flow control and management between SIS and application are local, not standardised in Annex A, and do not affect end-to-end interoperation; Annex S gives suitable primitives.
notes: We implement the Annex S local primitives (plan 4.3).

requirement: The content and use of the SIS primitives are as given in A.2.2.1 to A.2.2.9.
S_BIND_REQUEST carries the requested SAP ID and the default service type.
notes: Rank removed in Ed4 (A.5 item 3); the S encoding keeps a RANK nibble set to 0.

requirement: A new client issues S_BIND_REQUEST when it first connects.
notes: Client duty (client library). Node side: see S interp rows on primitives before bind.

requirement: A client that has not bound cannot be served; binding declares it on-line.
The first argument of S_BIND_REQUEST is the SAP ID the client wants.
A SAP ID is unique within the node: it cannot be given to a second client of the same node.
notes: Node enforces with S_BIND_REJECTED reason 3.

requirement: The last argument of S_BIND_REQUEST is the default Service Type, defined in A.2.2.6.
notes: Shall numbering jumps from (3) to (7) where Ed3 rank text was removed.

requirement: The bind Service Type applies to every U_PDU the client submits unless that U_PDU explicitly overrides it.
A client goes off-line by issuing S_UNBIND_REQUEST.
notes: Client duty.

requirement: On S_UNBIND_REQUEST the SIS releases the client's SAP ID.
A released SAP ID becomes available to any other client that asks for it.
A client that unbound can come back on-line with a new S_BIND_REQUEST.
notes: Basis for keeping the TCP connection open after unbind (S interp).

requirement: Disconnecting physically (for example powering off or unplugging) also takes a client off-line.
notes: Over TCP: connection close counts as unbind (S interp).

requirement: S_BIND_ACCEPTED is the SIS's positive response to S_BIND_REQUEST.
The SAP ID argument of S_BIND_ACCEPTED is the SAP ID assigned to the client.
That SAP ID equals the one in the S_BIND_REQUEST being answered.
The MTU argument tells the client the largest U_PDU, in bytes, it may submit in S_UNIDATA_REQUEST.
S_UNIDATA_REQUESTs whose U_PDU exceeds the MTU are rejected.
notes: See the over-MTU interp row.

requirement: U_PDUs received over the air are delivered to clients whatever their size; the MTU limit applies only to client submissions.
A general-purpose node uses an MTU of 2048 bytes.
A broadcast-only node has a configurable MTU.
reason: our node is general-purpose, not broadcast-only

requirement: A broadcast-only node's MTU does not exceed 4096 bytes.
reason: our node is general-purpose, not broadcast-only

requirement: S_BIND_REJECTED is the SIS's negative response to S_BIND_REQUEST.
The Reason argument of S_BIND_REJECTED states why the bind failed.
Bind reject reasons: 1 Not Enough Resources, 2 Invalid SAP ID, 3 SAP ID already allocated, 4 ARQ Mode unsupportable during Broadcast Session.
notes: Reason 4 is never sent by us (no exclusive broadcast session).

requirement: These bind reject values are the ones carried in the Annex S encoding.
The SIS uses S_UNBIND_INDICATION to declare a client off-line on its own initiative.
A client declared off-line must send a new S_BIND_REQUEST to come back.
notes: Text points to "A.2.1.1" for the bind; that is stale, the bind is A.2.2.1.

requirement: The Reason argument of S_UNBIND_INDICATION says why the client was taken off-line.

Unbind reasons: 1 Reserved, 2 Inactivity (no answer to keep-alive), 3 Too many invalid primitives, 4 Reserved, 5 ARQ Mode Unsupportable during Broadcast, 6 SIS service or session terminating (label garbled).
notes: Ed1 meanings of 1 (pre-empted by higher ranked client) and 4 (too many expedited requests) dropped with rank and expedited data.

requirement: These unbind reason values are the ones carried in the Annex S encoding.

The label of unbind reason 6 is printed run together ("SIS ServiceSession Terminating"). Reading: reason 6 means the node's SIS service is shutting down; the node sends it to every bound client before closing their connections on shutdown.
notes: Not in plan 4.4. Node.Shutdown is the host's last call before it destroys the core; in connection order, unbind reason 6 to each bound client, then every connection closed. Not a T2 input kind.

requirement: Unbind reasons 1 and 4 are Reserved in Ed4. Reading: the node never sends them; the client library treats any unknown or reserved reason as a generic unbind.
Bound clients submit U_PDUs for delivery with S_UNIDATA_REQUEST.
The Priority argument is the priority of the U_PDU.
Priority takes values 0 to 15, 0 lowest and 15 highest.
notes: Ed1 did not say which end was highest.

requirement: All HF sublayers make a best effort to give queued higher-priority U_PDUs precedence over lower-priority ones.
notes: Priority precedence is P6-2: the planner places queued data highest priority first, then oldest, whichever client sent it (C-0853); the SIS adds nothing to it.

requirement: The Destination SAP ID argument names the receiving client's SAP.
The Destination Node Address argument is the HF subnetwork address of the node the receiving client is bound to.
notes: May be a group address for non-ARQ only (Ed4 S.5.16.1).

requirement: The Delivery Mode (Service Type) argument has four elements: transmission mode, delivery confirmation, delivery order and minimum retransmissions.
notes: Annex S adds a fifth subfield, the Extended Field (Ed4 S.5.16.2).

requirement: Delivery Mode may be DEFAULT, meaning the Service Type given at bind; any other value overrides the bind default for this U_PDU.
notes: Encoded as Transmission Mode 0 (Ed4 S.5.16.2).

requirement: The transmission mode, ARQ or non-ARQ, is specified, with a non-ARQ submode when non-ARQ is chosen.
Non-ARQ has two submodes: error-free-only delivery (the default) and delivery-with-errors.
notes: We support error-free-only.

requirement: The delivery-with-errors submode is optional and belongs to the NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS profile option.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: A client may ask for no delivery confirmation, node-to-node, client-to-client, or both.
notes: Annex S can only carry one type per request (next rows).

requirement: Explicit delivery confirmation is requested only together with ARQ delivery.
notes: Client duty; node handling of violations in S interp rows.

requirement: Node-to-node confirmation reuses the DTS ARQ acknowledgement and adds no SIS peer traffic; client-to-client confirmation needs SIS peer S_PDUs and adds overhead.
Client-to-client confirmation should be used only when it is critical for the client to know its data reached the destination client.
notes: Client guidance (note); repeated in Ed4 S.5.3 p.S-12.

requirement: Annex A allows both confirmation types together, but the Annex S encoding allows only one per request.
notes: Ed4 S Fig S-6 value 11 is "not defined".

requirement: A client asks for either in-order delivery (as submitted) or delivery in the order received at the destination node.
In-order delivery is not requested for the non-ARQ service.
notes: New in Ed4 (A.5 item 6). Node handling of violations in S interp rows.

requirement: Avoid in-order delivery and handle ordering inside the application, because DTS in-order delivery couples different clients and can lose data needlessly.
notes: Client guidance ("recommended").

requirement: The Minimum Number of Retransmissions element is valid only when the transmission mode is a non-ARQ type.
For non-ARQ, the subnetwork retransmits each U_PDU the requested number of times.
If no retransmission count is given, the U_PDU is sent once.
notes: P3-1 carries the count to the DTS; sending is P3-4.

requirement: Retransmit the number of times specified plus "0 means sent once" [Ed4 A.2.2.6 p.A-9; S.5.3 p.S-12; S.5.16.2 p.S-20]. Reading: a count of N gives N+1 transmissions of the U_PDU in total.
notes: Cross-check with the Annex C non-ARQ repetition procedure in the C matrix. P3-1 carries the count to the DTS; the repeats are P3-4.

requirement: The TimeToLive argument is the longest time the U_PDU may stay in the subnetwork before delivery.
notes: Field unit and range in Ed4 S.5.12 (2 s, max 648000).

requirement: A U_PDU whose TTL is exceeded is discarded.
notes: P3-1 fixes the TTD; discarding on expiry is the DTS (P3-4) and receipt (P6-1).

requirement: TTL 0 means an infinite TTL: the subnetwork keeps trying to deliver.
notes: Conflicts with the TTD rule below; see interp.

requirement: The subnetwork has a default maximum TTL.
The default maximum TTL is configurable and implementation-dependent.
On accepting S_UNIDATA_REQUEST, the SIS at once computes the TimeToDie as current time plus TTL, or plus the default maximum when TTL is 0.
The TTD travels with the U_PDU through the subnetwork.
notes: TTD is absolute; TTL is relative to submission.

requirement: TTL 0 is "infinite" yet the same paragraph computes the TTD from the default maximum when TTL is 0 [Ed4 A.2.2.6 p.A-9]; the field maximum is 648000 x 2 s, about 15 days [Ed4 S Fig S-15, p.S-15]. Reading: TTL 0 = the configured default maximum, which we set to the field maximum.
notes: Plan 4.4.

requirement: The Size of U_PDU argument is the size of the U_PDU in this request.
The final U_PDU argument is the data the client submits.
The SIS issues S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM to acknowledge successful delivery of a submitted U_PDU.
S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM is issued only when the client asked for delivery confirmation, at bind or for that U_PDU.
The confirm's Destination Node Address equals that of the request it answers.
notes: Shall number (3) missing in the source.

requirement: The confirm's Destination SAP ID equals that of the request it answers.
The confirm's size argument is the size of the U_PDU, or U_PDU part, it carries.
The confirm's U_PDU argument is a copy of the whole U_PDU or of a fragment of it.
Depending on implementation, the returned copy may be only the first X bytes of the U_PDU.
A partial copy consists of U_PDU_response_frag_size bytes taken from the start of the U_PDU.
U_PDU_response_frag_size is configurable.
Confirms carry no request identifier; clients identify the U_PDU from destination, SAP and the returned bytes, which usually suffices.
notes: Plan 10.2 matching rule. Ed1 said the client "shall" be able to identify it; Ed4 says "usually".

requirement: The SIS issues S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED to tell a client a submitted U_PDU was not delivered.
S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED is issued when the client asked for delivery confirmation and delivery failed.
S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED is also issued whenever a client submits a U_PDU larger than the MTU.
notes: See over-MTU interp row.

requirement: Reject reasons: 1 TTL Expired, 2 Destination SAP ID not bound, 3 Destination node not responding, 4 U_PDU larger than MTU, 5 Tx Mode not specified, 6 Broadcast Not Allowed, 7 Address Not Known, 8 No ALE Mapping for Address, 9 Soft Link Terminated for higher priority link, 10 Soft Link Terminated to share channel, 11 Idle Soft Link Terminated, 12 Rejected due to EMCON state, 13 Data Buffers Full, 14 Address not Routable, 15 Other.
notes: We never send 8 (no ALE) or 14 (no Annex R). Reasons 1 to 5 were in Ed1; A.5 item 4 says new ones were added.

requirement: These reject reason values are the ones carried in the Annex S encoding.
The reject's Destination Node Address equals that of the request it answers.
notes: Shall number missing in the source.

requirement: The reject's Destination SAP ID equals that of the request it answers.
The reject's size argument is the size of the U_PDU, or U_PDU part, it carries.
As with the confirm, the reject may carry only a partial copy of the U_PDU.
A partial copy in a reject consists of U_PDU_response_frag_size bytes from the start of the U_PDU.
U_PDU_response_frag_size for rejects is configurable.
notes: One setting serves confirms and rejects (our choice, same parameter name).

requirement: Over-MTU U_PDUs: A.2.2.3 and A.2.2.8 always reject [pp.A-6, A-10], but A.3.2.3 notifies only when delivery confirmation was requested [p.A-22]. Reading: always send S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED reason 4; A.2.2.8 is the more specific rule.
notes: Plan 4.4.

requirement: The SIS delivers each received U_PDU to its client with S_UNIDATA_INDICATION.
The indication's Priority is the U_PDU's priority.
The indication's Destination SAP ID is the SAP of the client receiving it.
The indication's Destination Node Address is the address the sender put on the U_PDU: normally the local node, or a group address the local node subscribes to.
Group addresses and their member nodes are defined by configuration.
notes: Node needs a configured group-membership list; no protocol for joining groups exists in A or S.

requirement: The indication's Transmission Mode is the mode the U_PDU was sent and received in: ARQ, non-ARQ, or non-ARQ with errors.
notes: We only ever report ARQ or non-ARQ.

requirement: The indication's Source SAP ID is the SAP of the sending client.
The indication's Source Node Address is the node address of the sending client.
The indication's size argument is the size of the delivered U_PDU.
The four error-description arguments are absent from the indication unless the transmission mode is non-ARQ with errors.
notes: We always omit them.

requirement: The four error-description arguments are present when the transmission mode is non-ARQ with errors.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Number of Blocks in Error equals the count of data blocks received in error and passed up.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Number of Blocks in Error gives the number of pairs in the block-error array.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Each block-error pair holds the location of an errored block in the U_PDU and its size.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Number of Non-Received Blocks equals the count of blocks missing from the U_PDU.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Number of Non-Received Blocks gives the number of pairs in the non-received array.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Each non-received pair holds the location of a missing block in the U_PDU and its size.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: The final argument of the indication holds the received user data.
Peer SIS sublayers communicate by exchanging S_PDUs.
Peer-to-peer S_PDU exchange is used for client data, including its confirmation.
Setting up or ending soft link or broadcast sessions needs no explicit SIS peer exchange.
Three S_PDU types are currently defined; more may be added later.
notes: Same paragraph also says "eight S_PDU types" (editorial leftover from Ed3).

requirement: Every S_PDU starts with a common first field, TYPE.
TYPE values: 0 DATA, 1 DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM, 2 DATA DELIVERY FAIL, 3 to 7 reserved.
notes: TYPE is the high nibble of byte 0 (Figs A-3, A-6, A-8).

requirement: Types 3 to 7 were used by Edition 3 and are reserved in Edition 4.
notes: Ed3 hard link S_PDUs are referenced from A.4.1 (Ed3 A.3.1.4 to A.3.1.7).

requirement: Handling of a received S_PDU of reserved type (3 to 15) is NOT STATED. Reading: discard it without reply and log it; this covers Ed3 hard link S_PDUs, which we do not support.
notes: Not in plan 4.4. The S_PDU codec reports types 3 to 15 as invalid_field.

requirement: The meaning and encoding of the other fields of each S_PDU follow its own subsection.
The SIS sends client data to its peer in a DATA S_PDU.
The DATA S_PDU is encoded per Figures A-2, A-3 and A-4 and the text.
A DATA S_PDU has two parts, the S_PCI first and then the client U_PDU.
notes: Shalls (3) to (5).

requirement: The first S_PCI field is the 4-bit TYPE, value 0, in byte 0 bits 7 to 4.
notes: Bit positions from Fig A-3, p.A-15.

requirement: The second S_PCI field is the 4-bit PRIORITY, in byte 0 bits 3 to 0.
PRIORITY equals the Priority argument of the client's S_UNIDATA_REQUEST.
The third S_PCI field is the 4-bit SOURCE SAP ID of the sending client, in byte 1 bits 7 to 4.
The fourth S_PCI field is the 4-bit DESTINATION SAP ID of the receiving client, in byte 1 bits 3 to 0.
S_PDUs carry no node addresses; lower sublayers convey source and destination.
DESTINATION SAP ID equals the Destination SAP ID argument of the client's request.
The fifth S_PCI field is the 1-bit CLIENT DELIVERY CONFIRM REQUIRED flag (1 yes, 0 no), in byte 2 bit 7.
The CLIENT DELIVERY CONFIRM REQUIRED flag follows the U_PDU's delivery mode, or the bind default when the request used DEFAULT.
notes: Set to 1 only for client-to-client confirmation.

requirement: The sixth S_PCI field is the 1-bit VALID TTD flag (1 yes, 0 no), in byte 2 bit 6, saying whether a valid TTD is present.
The seventh S_PCI field is two unused bits reserved for future use, byte 2 bits 5 and 4.
notes: Shall numbers (14) and (15) are used twice in this section.

requirement: The value of the two reserved S_PCI bits is NOT STATED for S_PDUs. Reading: send 0 and ignore on receipt, as Annex S does for NOT USED bits [Ed4 S.5.2, p.S-10].
The eighth and last S_PCI field is the TTD (TimeToDie) of the U_PDU.
The first four TTD bits (byte 2 bits 3 to 0) have meaning only when VALID TTD is 1.
notes: Without TTD these bits are NOT USED (Fig A-4).

requirement: The other 16 TTD bits (bytes 3 and 4) are present only when VALID TTD is 1, so the S_PCI is 5 bytes with a TTD and 3 bytes without.
The TTD is the Julian day-of-year modulo 16 and the GMT time in seconds after which an undelivered S_PDU is discarded; Julian day 1 is 1 January, up to 365 or 366.
The Julian day modulo 16 goes in the first four TTD bits, byte 2 bits 3 to 0.
The GMT seconds value loses its least significant bit, and the 16 remaining high bits go in TTD bytes 3 and 4, most significant first.
notes: Resolution 2 s. MSB-first per Fig A-3.

requirement: When VALID TTD is 1 the full 20-bit TTD is present and the receiver must honour it, discarding the U_PDU if the TTD passes before delivery.
notes: TTD on receipt is P6-1.

requirement: When VALID TTD is 0 the last two TTD bytes are absent and the receiver must not use a TTD; it delivers without regard to time.
GMT in seconds has no stated origin. Reading: seconds since 00:00 UTC of the TTD's Julian day (0 to 86399), so the 16-bit field holds that value divided by 2 (0 to 43199).
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: The TTD day is only day-of-year modulo 16, and day numbers restart at 1 after 365 or 366; how a receiver resolves it is NOT STATED. Reading: resolve the 4-bit day and the seconds to the instant T, later than 1 day before now and no later than 15 days after now, whose day-of-year modulo 16 matches; if two dates match (possible only across a year end) take the earlier; if none matches, the TTD has passed. Deliver only if T is later than now.
notes: Not in plan 4.4. 15 days is the TTL field maximum (648000 x 2 s). Fixed in review: the earlier reading (nearest match from 8 days back to 15 ahead) turned a TTD 15 days ahead into yesterday, so a maximum-TTL U_PDU would be discarded on arrival. TTD on receipt is P6-1.

requirement: Whether the sender sets VALID TTD is not fixed. Reading: every DATA S_PDU we send carries VALID TTD = 1 with the TTD computed at acceptance, since every accepted U_PDU has a finite TTD under the TTL 0 reading.
notes: Our choice; costs 2 bytes per S_PDU.

requirement: A DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM S_PDU is sent after a U_PDU, received in a DATA S_PDU with CLIENT DELIVERY CONFIRM REQUIRED = 1, is delivered to its client.
The DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM goes to the peer SIS that originated the DATA S_PDU.
The first part of a DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM is its S_PCI.
The second part is a full or partial copy of the delivered U_PDU.
The first S_PCI field is TYPE with value 1 (byte 0 bits 7 to 4).
The other DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM S_PCI fields equal the matching fields of the DATA S_PDU it answers: byte 0 bits 3 to 0 priority, byte 1 source SAP ID then destination SAP ID, copied unswapped.
notes: Layout from Fig A-6. The S_PCI is 2 bytes.

requirement: DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM byte 0 low nibble: the Ed4 figure and text make it Priority, equal to the DATA S_PDU [Ed4 A.3.1.2 p.A-17, Fig A-6], while Ed1 marks it NOT USED. Reading: send the DATA S_PDU priority; ignore the nibble on receipt.
notes: Plan 4.4.

requirement: The SIS receiving a DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM tells the originating client of success with S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM, per A.3.2.3.
A DATA DELIVERY FAIL S_PDU is sent after a U_PDU, received in a DATA S_PDU with CLIENT DELIVERY CONFIRM REQUIRED = 1, cannot be delivered to its client.
The first part of a DATA DELIVERY FAIL is its S_PCI.
The second part is a full or partial copy of the undelivered U_PDU.
The first S_PCI field is TYPE with value 2 (byte 0 bits 7 to 4).
The second S_PCI field is a 4-bit REASON (byte 0 bits 3 to 0): 1 Destination SAP ID not bound; 0 and 2 to 15 reserved.
The DATA DELIVERY FAIL SOURCE SAP ID and DESTINATION SAP ID equal those of the DATA S_PDU it answers (byte 1).
DATA DELIVERY FAIL byte 0 low nibble is labelled Priority in Fig A-8 but REASON in the text [Ed4 A.3.1.3 p.A-18]. Reading: follow the text; the nibble is REASON, as in Ed1.
notes: Plan 4.4.

requirement: The SIS receiving a DATA DELIVERY FAIL tells the originating client of failure with S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED, per A.3.2.3.

A.3.2.3 says the reject reason is "derived from" the DATA DELIVERY FAIL [p.A-24] but gives no mapping. Reading: DDF reason 1 maps to reject reason 2 (Destination SAP ID not bound); any other DDF reason maps to reject reason 15 (Other).
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: The node whose client or SIS first asks for a session is the caller (calling node); the remote node is the called node.
The SIS opens soft links according to the destinations of queued U_PDUs; the algorithms (queue lengths, priorities, source-destination sets) are implementation-dependent and outside the standard.
A soft link is always set up before ARQ data crosses the CAS.
In Multiple Simultaneous Peer Access or ALE 1:1 EXPLICIT CAS-1 mode, non-ARQ data is always sent without a soft link.
notes: Our case (MSPA).

requirement: In ALE 1:1 IMPLICIT CAS-1 mode a soft link is set up for all data.
reason: ALE 1:1 not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: When the CAS rejects non-ARQ data with "Physical Link Needed", the SIS sets up a soft link and resends it.
reason: only in ALE 1:1 IMPLICIT CAS-1 mode, not in our profile

requirement: Setting up a soft link session needs no explicit SIS peer handshake.
The calling SIS sets up the soft link implicitly by asking its CAS for a physical link to the remote node, per Annex B.
Once the physical link exists, both SIS peers declare the soft link session established.
notes: Both CASs inform their SIS. Text points to "A.3.2.4" for data exchange; that is stale, it is A.3.2.3.

requirement: Ending a soft link session needs no SIS peer exchange.
Either peer ends a soft link session by asking its CAS to break the physical link, per Annex B.
A called peer waits a configurable minimum time before ending a session on its own, to keep the protocol stable.
notes: The note repeats this as a should and says the value is set per network in operating procedures.

requirement: The caller normally ends the session based on its queue; the called side may end it to serve higher-priority data for another node.
When told the physical link is broken, the SIS declares the soft link session terminated.
Under MSPA the SIS can hold queues to several peers with open soft links, and may hand all their data to the DTS, which then handles priority and sharing between peers (Annex C 7.5.2).
notes: may is bold on the rendered page; was info.

requirement: Under Single Peer Access with several peers, queueing is done in the SIS (except ALE 1:1 EXPLICIT CAS-1), since only a few soft links can be open.
reason: Single Peer Access model not used; we run MSPA (main Table 2)

requirement: Single Peer Access: when higher-priority traffic arrives for another peer, the SIS closes the active link as soon as practical, respecting A.3.2.1.3.
reason: Single Peer Access model only; we run MSPA

requirement: Single Peer Access: with traffic for several peers, the SIS is fair and opens soft links to each in turn at reasonable intervals.
reason: Single Peer Access model only; we run MSPA

requirement: The SIS closes a soft link with the CAS C_PHYSICAL_LINK_BREAK primitive, giving reason Soft Link Terminated for higher priority link, Soft Link Terminated to share channel, or Idle Soft Link Terminated.

requirement: Data the DTS rejects comes back as D_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED to the CAS and then C_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED to the SIS.
When such a rejection is caused by soft link termination, its reason matches the reason the SIS gave for closing the link.
Balancing fast link switching against letting transfers finish is an implementation choice.
Multicast ALE needs the channel to itself, so all soft links close before multicast or broadcast data is sent.

requirement: Once any session exists, sublayers with client data exchange DATA S_PDUs using this protocol and the session's service characteristics.
The SIS discards any submitted U_PDU larger than the MTU given in S_BIND_ACCEPTED.
If an over-MTU U_PDU asked for client or node delivery confirmation, the SIS sends the client S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED with reason U_PDU Larger than MTU.
notes: Our reading extends this to every over-MTU U_PDU (interp at A.2.2.8).

requirement: The sender takes accepted U_PDUs and their service attributes from its queues by priority and other implementation-dependent criteria.
The sender encodes each retrieved U_PDU in a DATA S_PDU, carrying over its service attributes.
notes: Shall numbers (4) to (6) and (10) absent in the source.

requirement: The sender encodes the DATA S_PDU per the CAS C_Primitive interface of Annex B.
The DATA S_PDU goes in a C_UNIDATA_REQUEST whose priority is the one the client gave.
notes: A trailing "otherwise" in the source is an Ed3 leftover from expedited data.

requirement: The sender passes the C_Primitive to the CAS for transmission.
For node delivery confirmation, the SIS waits a configurable time for a CAS response.
Node confirmation: C_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM within the wait gives the client S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM.
Node confirmation: C_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED gives the client S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED, unless the CAS reason is Physical Link Needed.
On a Physical Link Needed rejection (expected only for non-ARQ), the SIS sets up a soft link and resubmits the C_UNIDATA_REQUEST.
reason: Physical Link Needed arises only in ALE 1:1 IMPLICIT CAS-1 mode, not in our profile

requirement: Node confirmation: if the wait ends with no CAS response, the client gets S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED with reason Destination Node Not Responding.
For client delivery confirmation, the SIS waits a configurable time for a response.
Client confirmation: when both a C_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM and a DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM S_PDU arrive within the wait, the client gets S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM.
Client confirmation: a CAS reject or a DATA DELIVERY FAIL within the wait gives the client S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED.
notes: Source says "either a" with one alternative (editorial).

requirement: That reject's REASON is derived from the DATA DELIVERY FAIL or the CAS reject received.
notes: Mapping in interp at A.3.1.3.

requirement: Client confirmation: if the wait ends with no response, the client gets S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED with reason Destination Node Not Responding.
After these steps the sending protocol for that DATA S_PDU is complete.

The confirmation wait times are configurable with no default, and a U_PDU can also reach its TTD while waiting. Reading: a U_PDU whose TTD passes before it is handed to the CAS is rejected with reason 1 (TTL Expired) when confirmation was requested; the configurable wait starts when the DATA S_PDU is passed to the CAS and its expiry gives reason 3.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: The receiving SIS accepts DATA S_PDUs from the CAS through C_Primitives, per Annex B.
The receiving SIS extracts the U_PDU, Destination SAP ID and other service attributes from the DATA S_PDU.
If no client is bound to the Destination SAP ID, the receiver discards the U_PDU.
Otherwise the receiver delivers the U_PDU to the client on that SAP with S_UNIDATA_INDICATION.
notes: Shall number (24) absent in the source.

requirement: If CLIENT DELIVERY CONFIRM REQUIRED is 1, the receiver provides delivery confirmation as below.
A client was bound: the receiver sends a DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM S_PDU to the sender.
No client was bound: the receiver sends a DATA DELIVERY FAIL S_PDU to the sender.
notes: Reason 1.

requirement: After these steps the receiving protocol for that DATA S_PDU is complete.

A received DATA S_PDU whose valid TTD has already passed must not be delivered (A.3.1.1), but the response is NOT STATED: DATA DELIVERY FAIL has only reason 1. Reading: discard it without a DATA DELIVERY FAIL; a sender that asked for confirmation times out with reason 3.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

A TTD needs a UTC day and time [Ed4 A.2.2.6, p.A-9; A.3.1.1, p.A-16], but the sans-IO core has no clock. Reading: configuration gives the UTC year, day-of-year and seconds-of-day of core time 0 (time.epoch_year, time.epoch_day, time.epoch_second); a request's TTD is its acceptance time plus the TTL, converted with Gregorian calendar arithmetic; the result is rounded down to a whole second and then to an even second by dropping the least significant bit (A-0163), so the encoded TTD is never later than the TTL allows.
notes: Added by P3-1; core-architecture.md section 3.1 and section 10 item 12.

requirement: NOT STATED: what happens to a client's queued U_PDUs when it unbinds or disconnects. Reading (coordinator ruling): U_PDUs from its SAP still held in the SIS, including ARQ requests waiting for a soft link, are discarded without any confirmation; C_PDUs already handed to the DTS run to completion or TTL expiry

The SIS reject reason for U_PDUs held for a failed link make is NOT STATED (B-0029). Reading: each held U_PDU that asked for node or client confirmation gets S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED with reason 3 (destination node not responding) when the call had no answer, and reason 15 (other) for a peer rejection; one that asked for none is discarded silently (A-0105). Maximum Physical Links In Use and peer reason 4 reject nothing: the SIS holds off (B-0028, B-0303)
notes: The copy in the rejection follows sis.frag_size (interp A-0341, P6-1)

requirement: When all data for a soft-linked node has been sent (A-0011) is NOT STATED in SIS terms. Reading: a soft link is idle while no ARQ U_PDU to the peer is outstanding (handed to the CAS and not yet confirmed or rejected); sis.soft_link_idle/<peer> runs while it is idle and restarts on each ARQ C_PDU received from the peer (ongoing communication, A.3.2.1.3 note); at expiry, a peer heard addressing this node during the wait (a valid D_PDU header from it to this node's own address, C-0833, in a burst that began no earlier than the wait's count) is ongoing communication too, since it may be part way through a C_PDU: the wait counts again from the end of the last burst it was heard in, and runs for what is left of the idle time from then (A.3.2.1.4 leaves the balance between switching soft links and letting transfers complete to the implementation); otherwise the SIS closes the link with Idle Soft Link Terminated. An expiry while a burst is being received (between burst_started and burst_ended) is decided at that burst's end, after the DTS has handled it, by the same rule: the burst in progress may hold more of the peer's C_PDU, and is counted if it began no earlier than the wait's count and carried a valid header from the peer to this node, so a burst addressed to this node restarts the wait from its end; meanwhile a C_PDU received from the peer restarts the wait and an ARQ U_PDU handed over stops it as usual (issue #88). Both caller and called node run it (the note says the caller normally ends the session, A-0198); a called node's close waits for its minimum hold (A-0326). An idle time of 0 closes the link as soon as it is idle (A-0013)
notes: A-0011, A-0013, A-0198, A-0205; sis.soft_link_idle_ms; issue #86 (M0LTE.S5066): without the heard rule a receiver closed the link while the peer was still sending a C_PDU slowed by losses. Only headers to this node count: a peer heard working another node is not communicating with this one (the A.3.2.1.3 note speaks of communication with the distant node), and counting it would hold an idle link open for as long as the peer is busy elsewhere (reviewer change). Issue #88: without the deferral an expiry part way through a peer's burst closed the link before that burst's headers were counted; the decision is delayed by at most one burst

requirement: The idle timeout, minimum hold and maximum session time are configurable with no value given (A-0011, A-0015, A-0197; the A.3.2.1.3 note leaves them to each network's operating procedures), but each rule is a shall: an idle soft link is terminated (A-0011), a session is not kept past the maximum while others wait (A-0014), and a called peer waits a minimum time (A-0197). Leaving them off would keep idle links open for good and, once cas.max_links or a peer's limit is reached, hold off other peers for good (B-0028, B-0412 ask again only when a link closes). Reading: sis.soft_link_idle_ms, sis.soft_link_min_hold_ms and sis.soft_link_max_ms default to null, and when null each is derived from the answer wait (dts.ack_wait_ms or its derived value, C-1120), as B-0420 derives the CAS timers: the idle time three answer waits, an ARQ exchange that may need a retransmission (the peer's reply to our last U_PDU, or the caller's next C_PDU to a called node); the minimum hold three answer waits, the called node's wait for the first DATA C_PDU (cas.first_data, B-0420), so the caller has its first exchange before the called node may close on its own; the maximum session six answer waits, twice the minimum hold. A network sets its own values in its configuration
notes: Section 10 item 11 of core-architecture.md; T4 may recommend values. Reviewer change: null first turned the rules off

requirement: A-0014 does not say which U_PDUs are of suitable priority, nor what queued for other nodes means under MSPA, where the SIS hands data for every open soft link to the DTS (A-0200). Reading: U_PDUs held in the SIS for a peer that is held off because no link can be made (Maximum Physical Links In Use, locally or as the peer's reason 4, B-0028, B-0303), of any priority, since the DTS orders traffic by priority across links. sis.soft_link_max/<peer> starts when the soft link is established; once it has expired, the link is closed with Soft Link Terminated to share channel as soon as such U_PDUs are held (at once if they already are). One link is closed for each held-off peer waiting, less links the SIS is already closing, earliest established first, then lowest address

The called side may end a session to serve higher-priority data for another node (A-0198), and Soft Link Terminated for higher priority link is a close reason (A-0205), but the MSPA rule for it is NOT STATED (A-0202 is for Single Peer Access). Reading: when U_PDUs held off for another peer (as in A-0322) include one of priority p, and an open soft link has outstanding ARQ U_PDUs (A-0320) all of priority below p, that link is closed at once with Soft Link Terminated for higher priority link and priority p (B-0172), the lowest outstanding priority first, then earliest established, then lowest address. A link with nothing outstanding is left to its idle wait. Applies to caller and called node; a called node's close waits for its minimum hold (A-0326)

Which rejections are due to soft link termination (A-0207) is NOT STATED. Reading: the ARQ C_PDUs the DTS rejects because the connection ended (C-0652, C-0866), when the link was broken after a close the SIS asked for, including C_PDUs held back by the clean close (B-0246); the CAS gives each C_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED the reason the SIS gave, and the SIS answers a request that asked for confirmation with S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED reason 9, 10 or 11 (A-0105, A-0107) with the U_PDU cut to sis.frag_size (interp A-0341). A rejection for TTL expiry or a link lost keeps its own reason. An operator break has no SIS reject reason and keeps the no-connection reason. Other C_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED reasons are mapped by interp A-0340
notes: A-0105, A-0107, A-0205, A-0206, A-0207; B-0018 gives the C_ primitives no reason values

source: Ed4 A.3.2.1.3 p.A-20; B.2 Table B-1 pp.B-3 to B-4
requirement: The minimum hold applies to the called peer (A-0197), but Table B-1 gives C_PHYSICAL_LINK_MADE no parameters, so how the SIS knows its role is NOT STATED. Reading: C_PHYSICAL_LINK_MADE says whether this node is the called node of the link, which the CAS knows (B-0213, B-0219); in crossed calls the node whose PHYSICAL LINK ACCEPTED made the link is the called node (B-0405)

A-0197 does not say when the minimum hold starts or which closes it covers. Reading: sis.soft_link_min_hold/<peer> starts when the called node's soft link is established; while it runs the called node closes nothing on its own (idle, share channel or higher priority); an idle close that falls due meanwhile is made when the minimum hold expires, unless traffic has restarted the idle wait; a held-off peer's need is looked at again then. The caller has no minimum hold. A close by the peer or a link lost is not unilateral and is never held

NOT STATED: what the SIS does with ARQ U_PDUs that arrive for a peer whose soft link it is closing. Reading: they are held in the SIS, not handed down to a link that is being closed, and once the CAS reports the link broken a new soft link is asked for (A-0008); the held-off rules then apply as for any other U_PDU waiting for a link

The REASON of an S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED that answers a CAS reject is to be derived from it (A-0229), and Annex B names only TTL expiry and some local reasons as passed up to the SIS user (B-0031, B-0034). Rejections because the connection to the peer ended or never existed, and those of a soft link close, are not among them, and no mapping is given for them. Reading: TTL expired in the DTS gives 1 (TTL Expired), as B-0034 implies; a rejection caused by a soft link close the SIS asked for gives the close's reason, 9, 10 or 11 (A-0324); any rejection because the connection to the peer ended or never existed (the connection lost, a FULL RESET, an operator or peer break, no connection) gives 3 (Destination Node Not Responding)

U_PDU_response_frag_size is configurable for confirms and for rejects (A-0102, A-0114), and DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM and FAIL carry a full or partial copy (A-0172, A-0179) with no size given. Reading: one setting, sis.frag_size, cuts every copy the node makes: in S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM, in every S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED (over-MTU and every other reason) and in the DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM and FAIL S_PDUs it sends; a U_PDU no longer than the size is copied whole, and the size argument is the length copied (A-0098, A-0111). Null or absent copies the whole U_PDU
notes: M0LTE.S5066 issue #30 (null must mean a full copy)

requirement: The node and client confirmation waits are configurable with no value (A-0221, A-0226) and core timers cannot be named per U_PDU. Reading: one wait, sis.confirm_wait_ms, for both; it runs from when the DATA S_PDU is handed to the CAS (A-0232), and when it is null it ends at the U_PDU's TTD. A U_PDU that asked for confirmation and is still held for a soft link waits until its TTD, which drops it with reason 1 (A-0232). Every deadline is one entry in a list behind the single timer sis.confirm_wait (core-architecture.md 3.2, collapsing rule), ordered by deadline then insertion; at expiry a held U_PDU gets reason 1 and one handed down gets reason 3 (A-0225, A-0230). The record then ends: a later CAS answer or peer answer is ignored, though the DTS keeps the C_PDU. An unbind ends the waits of its SAP with no answer (A-0260). The answer to the client is sent before the timer output it causes

A DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM or FAIL carries no request identifier, and how the sending SIS matches it to a U_PDU is NOT STATED (A-0103 says only that clients can usually tell from the copy). Reading: it answers the oldest (by request handle) U_PDU handed to the CAS for the node it came from that asked for client confirmation and has no peer answer yet, whose source and destination SAP IDs equal those in the S_PDU and whose first bytes are the returned copy (an empty copy matches any); one that matches nothing is discarded. A confirm completes the confirmation once the CAS has confirmed, in either order (A-0227); a fail, or a CAS reject, rejects at once (A-0228)

How the receiving SIS sends a DATA DELIVERY CONFIRM or FAIL (A-0238, A-0239) is NOT STATED: the S_PDUs have no TTD, priority only in the confirm, and no delivery mode. Reading: it goes in a C_UNIDATA_REQUEST to the sender's own address, by ARQ when the DATA S_PDU came by ARQ (over the soft link, waiting for one like any ARQ U_PDU, and handed down even while the SIS is closing that soft link) and otherwise non-ARQ with no repeats; with the DATA S_PDU's priority, no in-order delivery, and the TTD of a U_PDU given TTL 0 (now plus sis.default_ttl); marked as a client confirmation so a clean close lets it start (B-0246, B-0318). An ARQ one is outstanding on its soft link like an ARQ U_PDU (A-0320), and its own rejection is told to nobody. A DATA S_PDU discarded for its TTD gets no answer (A-0241)
